minutes.headline: Water commissioners set the 2025 meeting schedule and heard an on-track early FY26 budget look, PFAS updates and a hydrant plan.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners approved the prior minutes and the 2025 meeting schedule, and heard a preliminary FY26 budget review in which the superintendent said spending is on track. Most of the meeting covered PFAS sampling and state regulation, the PFAS and hard water pilot study, and a proposal to have water staff on site when the fire department uses hydrants, to prevent pressure surges and main breaks.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked about the size of the supply line used at the John Street hydrant call and how the hydrant barrel fills.
A resident asked about the Massachusetts PFAS limit and whether the federal change would affect it, and urged educating the fire department to save overtime and materials.

votes.motion: Accept the Board of Water Commissioners meeting schedule for 2025.

budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said the budget draft awaits the auditor finishing; a fuller review and an executive session on raises are planned for the next meeting.
Health insurance is the main unknown, with possible increases of up to roughly ten percent.
Retirement costs have risen in past years and are being tracked to project next year.
Chemical costs dropped from 22 to 23 and 23 to 24; this year is running below the amount budgeted.
A July-to-date comparison from QuickBooks shows the district on budget.
A speaker said overtime and materials costs from hydrant-caused breaks make prevention worthwhile.

decisions.decision: The detailed FY26 budget review and executive session on raises will be held at the next meeting on the 18th.
Commissioners plan to tour the neighbouring water plant, tentatively on a Wednesday in late January.
Commissioners were supportive of trying to have water staff attend when the fire department uses hydrants.

what_happened.line: The Water District commissioners took up a motion to accept the 2025 meeting schedule; the recording does not make the outcome audible.
The superintendent gave a preliminary FY26 budget look: the district is on budget against the July-to-date comparison, with health insurance the main unknown.
The detailed FY26 budget review and an executive session on raises were put off to the next meeting on the 18th.
Commissioners were supportive of trying to have water staff on site when the fire department uses hydrants, to avoid pressure surges and main breaks.
The meeting also covered PFAS sampling and state regulation, and a PFAS and hard water treatment pilot study; both were informational.

why_it_matters: Water rates in the FY26 budget rest on costs the superintendent called unsettled, chiefly health insurance, so the 18th is when a resident can first see the full draft.
Hydrant-caused main breaks bring overtime and materials costs, so a staffing agreement with the fire department bears on what the district spends, and on what ratepayers cover, in repairs.
PFAS regulation and treatment work can add future capital and operating costs to the system, though no figure was set at this meeting.
